findings.finding: Frontend/backend contract mismatch renders the new evidence line broken: GET /admin/reports now returns `qualifyingInteraction` as a plain enum STRING (e.g. `"SHARED_CONVERSATION"`), per rentals/backend/src/routes/admin.ts's `...r` spread of the raw Prisma row and rentals/backend/prisma/schema.prisma's `qualifyingInteraction ReportQualifyingInteraction?` scalar column. The frontend (rentals/frontend/src/app/admin/page.tsx:389-398) was written against a guessed contract where `qualifyingInteraction` is an OBJECT with a `.type` sub-field and an optional `.listing.title` (`r.qualifyingInteraction.type === 'SHARED_CONVERSATION'`, `r.qualifyingInteraction.listing?.title`). Since `r.qualifyingInteraction` is actually a bare string, `.type` is always `undefined` on every branch, so every ternary falls through to the same `undefined` fallback and the moderator sees a blank/empty 'Qualifying interaction: ' line for every USER report, regardless of which path actually qualified it. This defeats the entire purpose of the task rather than being a no-op — it will actively render misleading, content-free output once the field is populated. This exact risk was flagged by the Frontend engineer's own report ('the exact field name/shape... is my proposal, not a confirmed contract with Backend... please reconcile') but the Integrator's merge reported 'no reconciliation was needed' and did not catch it since no overlapping files triggered manual review, and neither side's own tsc could catch it because `r` is loosely typed in the admin page.
findings.evidence: Backend: src/routes/users.ts:181-187 sets `qualifyingInteraction` to `ReportQualifyingInteraction.SHARED_CONVERSATION` etc. (a Prisma enum, serialized as a plain string), and admin.ts's `return { ...r, ... }` (~line 524) passes it through unmodified as a top-level string field. Frontend: src/app/admin/page.tsx:389-398 accesses `r.qualifyingInteraction.type` and `r.qualifyingInteraction.listing?.title`, which do not exist on a string.
findings.recommendedAction: Reconcile the contract: either (a) simplest fix — change the frontend to compare `r.qualifyingInteraction === 'SHARED_CONVERSATION'` etc. directly (matching what the backend actually sends), dropping the `.type`/`.listing` object shape entirely since the backend doesn't capture which specific listing was involved anyway, or (b) if per-listing detail is wanted, have backend additionally persist/return the specific listing id/title tied to the qualifying interaction and wrap it in an object server-side to match the frontend's shape. Route back to Frontend (or Backend+Frontend jointly) to fix and re-verify with a real admin-panel render (or at least a mocked API response) before this is considered complete.

findings.finding: Even after fixing the type mismatch, the LISTING_MESSAGED/LISTING_SAVED evidence will never include a listing title/id, since users.ts only records which enum path passed (`select: { id: true }` on the qualifying listing lookups) and discards the specific listing. The frontend's `.listing?.title` optional-chaining anticipates this data but it will never be populated under the current backend implementation.
findings.recommendedAction: Non-blocking polish: if per-listing detail is valuable to moderators, capture and persist the qualifying listing's id (and resolve title via the existing include) in a follow-up; otherwise simplify the frontend copy to not reference a listing title at all, since it can never appear.

notes: Reviewed the integrated worktree directly (git log confirms both implementer branches merged into agents/.../integration). Backend implementation itself (schema, migration, users.ts gate logic, admin.ts scalar passthrough) is sound, additive-only, correctly nullable, and matches the existing gate's precedence (SHARED_CONVERSATION > LISTING_MESSAGED > LISTING_SAVED). Authorization is unchanged (no new read/write surface). The blocking issue is purely the frontend/backend payload-shape mismatch described above, which was a known risk flagged by Frontend's own report but not resolved during integration. Verification level: CODE_REVIEWED only (no DB/dev server available in this worktree to run the flow end-to-end).
